I1.quote: H2 was admitted into the apparatus to a certain pressure (about 10 to 12 MPa) and the H2 adsorption began. The changes in pressure were monitored versus time.
I1.location: main, p. 2 (journal p. 1128), main text, right column

I2.quote: Three samples of SWNTs (each of ~500 mg in weight) were collected from a batch of as-prepared SWNTs, but were pretreated in three different ways, and then were denoted as sample 1, sample 2, and sample 3.
I2.location: main, p. 2 (journal p. 1128), main text, middle column

I3.quote: All samples were placed in the sample cell, heated at 423 K, degassed in vacuum for several hours, and then exposed to 100 to 120 atm of H2 at 298 K until equilibrium was achieved (typically 6 hours).

I4.quote: Searched text layer and page images pp. 1-4 (Table 1, Figs. 1-3, captions) for any specific surface area (BET, Langmuir, other method, supplier value, 'm2/g'); none found. Only TGA purity, HRSEM/HRTEM and Raman diameter are reported.

I5.quote: Masses of single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWNTs) with a large mean diameter of about 1.85 nanometers, synthesized by a semicontinuous hydrogen arc discharge method, were employed for hydrogen adsorption experiments in their as-prepared and pretreated states.
I5.location: main, p. 1 (journal p. 1127), abstract, first sentence

notes: Volumetric (pressure-change) uptake at 298 K for three arc-discharge SWNT samples: Table 1 gives 2.4, 2.8 and 4.2 wt% after exposure to 100-120 atm H2; Fig. 3 plots uptake (wt%) and dP/weight (atm/g) versus time, so the equilibrium pressure is stated only as the 100-120 atm (10-12 MPa) initial range; I3 judged met on that statement. I2: SWNT purity 50-60 wt% with ~40 wt% catalyst residue (Ni, Co, Fe) in the as-prepared product, so carbon is still the majority component by mass. No not_primary, retracted or duplicate_data indication: record.json is_retracted false, the PDF carries no retraction notice, and the paper does not state that its uptake values were published before. Exclusion is no_surface_area (I4) alone. PDF p. 1 begins with the end of an unrelated preceding article and p. 3 with the start of an unrelated following article (diatom silaffins); these were not assessed.
